questions.prompt: Which PVM idea is amplified, and which Scheme semantic decisions must stay out of C layout helpers?
questions.answer: Retain GVM target cooperation; one explicit frame/root origin feeds collectors and continuation consumers. The C role cut is groundwork, not a completed generator rewrite or LLVM backend.
questions.evidence: FeeleyMillerLFP90 sections 1-2; gambit.h.in context accessors; mem.c mark_execution_roots; frame-consumers.org
questions.counterexample: Recreating Scheme control semantics independently in a new backend duplicates the semantic authority; moving C fields alone does not amplify PVM optimization.

questions.prompt: Does the new root participant prove progress for nonallocating loops, foreign blocking calls and collector cooperation?
questions.answer: No. This cut keeps the existing synchronous safepoint mechanism; phase guards establish ordering only. A bounded-progress claim needs generator placement, root freeze and foreign participation together.
questions.evidence: Feeley1993 via retro-parallel section 3.4; mem.c require_gc_phase and garbage_collect_pstate; modernization-target.org
questions.counterexample: A nonallocating spin loop can avoid allocation checks and prevent a collective; new phase enums cannot force it to participate.

questions.prompt: Can captured map frames be resumed repeatedly after GC without consuming roots or imposing one-shot ownership?
questions.answer: Shared frame/root traversal is source groundwork; the new generated runtime cohort and real repeated-resume acceptance are missing.
questions.evidence: mem.c mark_continuation; existing frame decoder; retro-concurrency sections 4-5 distinguish one-shot fibers
questions.counterexample: Treating a captured frame as uniquely consumed after its first resume preserves an OCaml-style use case but breaks Scheme multi-shot behavior.

questions.prompt: What actually breaks the dependency on a terminating processor carrier?
questions.answer: Storage and call paths are separated, but cleanup_pstate still cleans context resources and allocator/logging still borrow a synchronous carrier; independent retirement is not implemented.
questions.evidence: setup.c cleanup_pstate; mem.c worker carrier uses; runtime-role-realization.sysml RR-LIFETIME
questions.counterexample: Clearing carrier bytes leaves a VM array intact but does not prove that a thread or context can retire while users remain.

questions.prompt: Can every RC/root writer, native callback and foreign destructor coexist with root freeze and worker completion without a wait cycle?
questions.answer: Per-participant RC scan origins are explicit; all-writer freeze, callback escape and destructor progress remain unqualified.
questions.evidence: mem.c mark_rc and free_unmarked_still_objs; setup.c run/catcher/cleanup; native failure evidence RR-LIFETIME
questions.counterexample: GC waits for an owner callback while the owner waits for GC completion; a correct root array does not eliminate the cycle.

questions.prompt: Who retains roots and work after partial startup, failed join, unknown exit or a missing final acknowledgement?
questions.answer: Closed-round publication and readback are modeled; complete source/barrier/failure custody and actual native fault controls are open.
questions.evidence: mem.c gc_round and final barrier; runtime_roles.qnt; setup.c resize cleanup; registered repair-9-12 evidence
questions.counterexample: A two-participant model assumes both members reach their barriers; a failed native participant can prevent that premise.

questions.prompt: Which work is removed now, what is added, and what would refute a net-benefit claim?
questions.answer: Old carrier fields, implicit root origin and collector queue selection are replaced. The recorded 64-slot VM grows 3080 bytes; root indirection and one final collective are added. No runtime speedup is measured.
questions.evidence: matched parent/current sizeof; runtime-role-matrix.org; source commit diff; verification.json
questions.counterexample: A smaller carrier is not a smaller VM. If downstream retirement never occurs, extra indirection and coordination can exceed the value of the split.

questions.prompt: Which old responsibilities actually disappear, and is any patch result being presented as refactoring acceptance?
questions.answer: Direct carrier root/memory fields and old visitor trio are removed; embedded C consumers change. Cleanup lifecycle and generated cohort are open. Bazel provides configuration; patch receipts remain separate historical observations with 8/12 unchanged.
questions.evidence: negative old-field compile; source diff; runtime-role-realization.org; historical SMP observation
questions.counterexample: Importing patch candidates or labeling historical passes with the new source SHA does not retire ownership or establish native acceptance.
